title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is a ring and L_. is a simplicial k-module. Here '½ simplicial' should be read in the older sense of 'semi-simplicial', i.e. simplicial with degeneracies. The page uses the Dold-Puppe (Dold-Kan) correspondence, which needs degeneracies, and next page's formula for L_n has binomial ranks; both support this reading. The page sits in a classification project: 'dévissage' of '∂-perfect' simplicial complexes (and later multiplicative structures).

Two basic simplicial k-modules are used.
- Φ: by the rank count, Φ_n = k^{n+1}. Its normalized complex is k --id--> k in degrees 1 and 0, so it is contractible. A model is the pointed linearized Δ^1, i.e. k[Δ^1]/k[vertex].
- Ψ: Ψ_n = k^n, with normalized complex k in degree 1, so Ψ = K(k,1). A model is the reduced linearized simplicial circle Δ^1/∂Δ^1.
- Taking exterior powers degreewise: Λ^iΦ_n has rank C(n+1,i) = C(n,i) + C(n,i-1), and its normalized complex is the 'disk' (k → k) in degrees i, i-1. Λ^jΨ_n has rank C(n,j), and its normalized complex is the 'sphere' k[j]; so Λ^jΨ is literally the Dold-Kan model of K(k,j), and Λ^0Ψ = k is constant.
- Why these complexes are as claimed: by décalage, Λ^j(K(k,1)) has homotopy k concentrated in degree j. Dold-Kan gives L_n ≅ ⊕_p N_p^{C(n,p)}. Uniqueness of binomial expansions of ranks then forces N_p = 0 for p ≠ j.

Proposition. For a simplicial k-module L the following are equivalent:
- (a) all L_n and all π_n(L) are projective;
- (a') all components N(L)_n of the Dold-Puppe chain complex L^! and all H_n(L^!) are projective;
- (b) L ≅ ∏_{i≥1} Λ^iΦ_k ⊗ M_i × ∏_{j≥0} Λ^jΨ_k ⊗ N_j;
- (b') L^! ≅ ∏_{i≥1} (M_i --id--> M_i in degrees i, i-1) × ∏_{j≥0} (N_j in degree j).
The M_i and N_j are unique up to isomorphism and the same in (b) and (b'). Explicitly N_j ≅ H_j(L) = π_j and M_i ≅ L_i/Z_i ≅ B_{i-1}.
Products can replace sums because the product is degreewise finite: Λ^iΦ_n = 0 for i > n+1 and Λ^jΨ_n = 0 for j > n. This is exactly next page's formula for L_n.

Proof as sketched.
- (a')⇔(b'): the standard splitting of a nonnegatively graded complex of projectives with projective homology. Inductively, Z_0 = N_0 is projective; then B_0 is projective, being the kernel of the split surjection Z_0 → H_0. Next Z_1 = ker(N_1 → B_0) is projective as the kernel of a split surjection, and so on.
- (a)⇔(a'): from L_n ≅ ⊕_p N_p^{C(n,p)}, and N_p is a direct summand of L_p.
- (b)⇔(b'): Dold-Kan is an equivalence of categories, together with the computation of N(Λ^iΦ) and N(Λ^jΨ).

The proposition serves next page's Cor 1 and Cor 2: finite type, and finitely many nonzero M_i, N_j. Those characterize 'perfect' simplicial modules as (direct summands of) finite products of such exterior-power models. The exterior-power description is presumably chosen with later multiplicative (λ-type) structures in mind.
errors: (b') speaks of 'complexes de cochaînes', but the complexes are chain complexes (M_i in degrees i and i-1, homological). This is a slip of wording.

The proof leaves implicit the key computation that the normalized complex of Λ^jΨ is exactly k[j] and that of Λ^iΦ is exactly the disk. It is true, but it is the only non-formal input (décalage plus the rank argument).

With 'somme' replaced by 'produit', infinitely many nonzero factors are harmless because each degree involves only finitely many. The text does not say this, though it is implicit in next page's formula.

ideas.what: Simplicial modules with projective components and projective homotopy split, as simplicial modules, into products of Eilenberg-MacLane pieces K(N_j,j) and contractible pieces.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of chain complexes of projectives with projective homology, transported by the Dold-Kan correspondence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold, Kan, Dold-Puppe (1958-61); standard homological algebra

ideas.what: Explicit strict models: the Dold-Kan model of K(k,j) is the j-th degreewise exterior power of the simplicial circle module Ψ (Ψ_n = k^n). The contractible disk on degrees i, i-1 is Λ^i of the linearized pointed interval Φ (Φ_n = k^{n+1}).
ideas.modern_name: Exterior powers of simplicial modules / décalage (LΛ^j(M[1]) ≃ LΓ^j(M)[j])

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the multiplicities: N_j ≅ H_j, M_i ≅ B_{i-1}.

missed.claim: A strict (not merely up-to-homotopy) presentation of every 'projective' simplicial module as a product of exterior powers Λ^iΦ⊗M_i and Λ^jΨ⊗N_j of two universal simplicial modules. This sets up a λ-ring / multiplicative-structure treatment of perfect simplicial modules, which the surrounding manuscript pursues. The equivalence itself is routine; the exterior-power packaging is a mildly distinctive viewpoint, but probably known in substance.
missed.quote: L_. est isomorphe à un produit direct de C de la forme (∏_{i≥1} Λ^iΦ_k ⊗_k M_i) × ∏_{j≥0}(Λ^jΨ_k)⊗_k N_j
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives explicit generators for K_0-type and λ-structure questions on simplicial perfect modules. Its interest depends on what the rest of manuscript 137 does with it.

deep.surprise_reason: The equivalence is a standard consequence of Dold-Kan plus the splitting of projective complexes; Grothendieck himself calls (a')⇔(b') 'trivial et bien connu'. The only slightly notable point is the strict identification of the Dold-Kan Eilenberg-MacLane models with exterior powers of the simplicial circle and interval, which is known in substance via décalage.
transcription_corrections: '(b) ... Φ_{*k}' and 'Ψ_{*k}' should probably read Φ_k, Ψ_k (Φ, Ψ base-changed to k), consistent with the next page's Φ_{n,k}.
In (b') the first factor is (0 → M_i → M_i → 0 → …) with the identity map. The '?' superscript is a degree label, with the brace reading 'en degré i et i-1'.
'(vu le) topos de Dold-Puppe' is doubtful; most likely 'vu la théorie (or le théorème) de Dold-Puppe'.
The final words 'et la démonstration concluante est complète' are uncertain. The sense is 'd'où l'équivalence des 4 conditions, et la démonstration est complète'.
In (b) the struck word above is 'somme', replaced by 'produit', and 'de modules' is struck. The earlier 'b)' label in the second condition is 'a')'.
